question: Can diffusion models be endowed with a non-degenerate information geometry by treating every noisy state and time as a point indexing the reverse-SDE denoising posterior, and does this geometry yield meaningful image edit distances and efficient molecular transition paths?

key_findings.claim: For a bijective same-dimensional PF-ODE decoder equipped with the decoder's Euclidean pullback metric, every globally shortest latent path decodes to a straight segment and its length is the ambient Euclidean endpoint distance.
key_findings.evidence: The pullback curve length equals the Euclidean length of its decoded image by the chain rule. Because the decoder is bijective, the inverse image of the constant-speed straight segment exists and attains the Euclidean lower bound. The theorem is correct under its assumptions, but it is a general coordinate-change fact rather than a diffusion-specific pathology; it does not invalidate pullbacks through non-bijective feature maps, lower-dimensional representations, density-weighted metrics, or non-Euclidean output metrics.

anchors.section: 4 Pullback Geometry Collapses in Diffusion Models, Equations 9-10
Appendix B, Lemma B.1 and Proposition B.1

key_findings.claim: The central information-geometric construction is an exact and useful reduction: denoising posteriors across state and time form an exponential family with explicit natural and expectation coordinates.
key_findings.evidence: Bayes' rule with Gaussian forward corruption gives base measure h(x0)=q(x0), sufficient statistic T(x0)=(x0, ||x0||^2), and natural coordinate eta(xt,t)=(alpha_t xt/sigma_t^2, -alpha_t^2/(2 sigma_t^2)). The expectation coordinate is (E[x0|xt], E[||x0||^2|xt]). This converts the Fisher tensor into (d eta/dz)^T(d mu/dz) on spacetime z=(xt,t).

anchors.section: 5 Information Geometry with Denoising Decoders, Proposition 5.1
Appendix C.1, Fisher geometry of exponential families

key_findings.claim: The discrete curve objective has a principled exact-divergence interpretation when eta and mu are exact, but the implemented denoiser-based objective is only an approximation to that geometry.
key_findings.evidence: For adjacent points, the paper uses one half times the dual-coordinate inner product Delta eta^T Delta mu for energy and its square root for length. Appendix D shows that the corresponding pair term is the symmetrized KL divergence for exact members of an exponential family, not merely a local Taylor term. In implementation, however, mu is obtained from an approximate denoiser and a stochastic divergence estimate, so the exact dual-coordinate and divergence identities need not hold numerically.

anchors.section: Appendix D, Lemmas D.1-D.2 and Equation 63

key_findings.claim: The proposed simulation-free estimator replaces reverse-SDE rollouts with denoiser evaluations and one Hutchinson JVP per curve point, but its numerical validity is not audited.
key_findings.evidence: Tweedie's formula estimates the posterior mean, while the second moment is reconstructed as the squared denoiser output plus sigma_t^2/alpha_t times its divergence. Listing 1 draws one Rademacher probe and computes one JVP. The paper reports no bias, variance, probe-count sensitivity, repeated-estimate agreement, or check that Delta eta^T Delta mu remains nonnegative under an imperfect denoiser. The listing also calls pred_f after defining pred_fn, an apparent implementation typo in the printed pseudocode.

key_findings.claim: The clean-data distance is defined at a singular boundary, whereas every practical experiment measures an implementation-dependent distance between noised or PF-ODE-encoded endpoints at t_min greater than zero.
key_findings.evidence: The formal definition identifies a clean datum with the Dirac posterior at (x,0), but local KL and Fisher quantities diverge or become unstable near that boundary. DiffED therefore anchors endpoints at t_min>0; image pairs are first encoded through StabilityVAE and then integrated by PF-ODE to t_min=0.368. Other experiments use different t_min values. Thus practical values depend on t_min, noise schedule, VAE and PF-ODE encoding, denoiser checkpoint, discretization, and optimizer rather than solely on two clean images.

anchors.section: The latent spacetime and clean-data identification

key_findings.claim: The computed curves are locally optimized cubic splines, not certified global geodesics, so the numerical DiffED is not established as a metric.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithms 3-4 initialize one cubic spline and minimize a discretized stochastic energy with gradient descent or Adam/AdamW. Experiments use hand-chosen node counts, discretizations, learning rates, iteration budgets, and no multiple-start or convergence protocol. The paper provides no global-optimality guarantee, discretization limit, endpoint-symmetry test, triangle-inequality test, identity-of-indiscernibles test, or optimizer uncertainty. A low objective is therefore evidence for a candidate path, not proof of the shortest path.

key_findings.claim: On ImageNet-512, optimizing PF-ODE sampling trajectories changes them only marginally and cannot itself produce an alternative sampler.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 reports that optimized geodesics are almost indistinguishable from the original EDM2 PF-ODE paths, with information appearing only slightly earlier. The authors explicitly note that both endpoints must already be known. Optimizing one trajectory takes roughly two hours on an A100 because 600 AdamW steps are needed and larger learning rates yield NaNs.

key_findings.claim: The image evidence does not validate DiffED as a perceptual distance or demonstrate downstream utility.
key_findings.evidence: Across 200 random within-class ImageNet pairs from ten classes, DiffED correlates approximately -7% with LPIPS and 53% with SSIM; no human judgments, confidence intervals, correlation type, metric-axiom checks, cross-class analysis, retrieval task, robustness study, or learned-distance baseline is reported. The only ranking visualization uses 20 pairs from the single class 'Space bar.' Computing one interpolation takes about six minutes on an A100 with the XXL checkpoint, compared with essentially immediate LPIPS or SSIM evaluation.

key_findings.claim: The alanine experiment reports a numerically strong maximum-energy result and favorable energy-evaluation count within the authors' chosen benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: For 1,000 paths in two-dimensional dihedral space, the method reports MaxEnergy 37.36±0.60 against a numerical lower bound of 36.42, versus 42.54±7.42 for fixed-length MCMC, 58.11±18.51 for variable-length MCMC, and 66.24±1.01 for the authors' Doob implementation. It uses 16.385 million per-path-generation energy-gradient evaluations plus 16 million one-time evaluations to create diffusion training samples, compared with 1.29 billion, 21.02 million, and 38.4 million for those baselines.

anchors.section: Appendix G.3, data and diffusion training

key_findings.claim: The molecular experiment does not yet establish physically correct transition-path sampling or a general advantage over contemporary molecular path samplers.
key_findings.evidence: Alanine is reduced to its two dihedral angles and the original potential is replaced with a 2×64 neural surrogate trained on 16,384 grid locations to MSE about 1.5. Evaluation uses only maximum surrogate energy, not path-distribution likelihood, Onsager-Machlup action, committor consistency, transition rates, kinetics, full-atom feasibility, or diversity. The annealed sequence of conditional Boltzmann distributions is not shown to reproduce the conditioned molecular dynamics whose rare paths are sought.

key_findings.claim: The baseline comparison is unusually transparent about reproduction failures, but those failures make its state-of-the-art claim unreliable and its compute accounting incomplete.
key_findings.evidence: Holdijk and Raja are excluded because their alanine results could not be reproduced or were absent; official Doob code yielded much worse results than the publication despite a broad configuration search, and the best failed reproduction is reported. The authors' count focuses on energy evaluations and separates diffusion-data generation, while omitting surrogate-energy training, diffusion training, denoiser/JVP work, and 10,000-step geodesic optimization; baseline counts need not include analogous cost categories. This is a useful diagnostic, not a controlled comparison to published performance.

anchors.section: Appendix G.3, auxiliary and diffusion-model training

key_findings.claim: Low-variance and region-avoidance constraints demonstrate flexible differentiable path penalties, but only qualitatively and with substantial manual tuning.
key_findings.evidence: The framework adds an SNR-based low-variance penalty and a KL-based restricted-region penalty to the curve energy. Figure 7 shows plausible path shifts, but there are no quantitative satisfaction rates, coverage or diversity measures, energy trade-off curves, or robustness to thresholds. Appendix G.3 reports hand-selected rho and lambda schedules, and region avoidance additionally requires a low-variance term to prevent the trivial high-entropy solution.

method.core_idea: Replace a degenerate geometry on terminal diffusion noise with the Fisher-Rao geometry of the entire family of denoising posteriors indexed by noisy state and time. Use exponential-family dual coordinates to evaluate curve energy without reverse-SDE simulations, optimize shortest candidate curves, and reuse them as image edit paths or annealing schedules for molecular transitions.
method.mechanism: First prove that the Euclidean pullback through the bijective PF-ODE decoder merely reparameterizes ambient Euclidean data geometry. For the stochastic reverse-SDE decoder, define each spacetime point z=(xt,t) by p(x0|xt). Gaussian forward corruption makes this posterior family exponential with explicit eta and sufficient statistic (x0,||x0||^2). Approximate the expectation coordinate mu with a denoiser, Tweedie's identities, and a Hutchinson divergence estimate. Discretize cubic-spline curves, minimize sums of Delta eta^T Delta mu, and define DiffED from the resulting length. For a Boltzmann target, interpret each spacetime point as a conditional Boltzmann density and anneal Langevin dynamics along the optimized curve. Add differentiable SNR or KL penalties for constrained paths.
assumptions: The PF-ODE decoder is bijective and smooth enough that its inverse maps the Euclidean line segment to an admissible latent curve.
The output metric used in the pullback theorem is the ambient Euclidean metric, not a perceptual, feature, density, uncertainty, or task-specific metric.
The forward kernel is isotropic Gaussian with known alpha_t and sigma_t and the data distribution admits the conditional densities used in the exponential-family derivation.
Terminal diffusion is sufficiently memoryless that p(x0|xT) is effectively independent of xT, while intermediate times preserve usable posterior variation.
The pretrained denoiser accurately estimates E[x0|xt] and its JVP is reliable at all spacetime points visited during optimization.
One Hutchinson probe supplies a sufficiently stable divergence estimate in high-dimensional latent image space.
Approximate eta and mu remain dual-consistent enough that every pair contribution is nonnegative and behaves like symmetrized KL.
A finite discretized cubic spline found from one initialization is close enough to the globally shortest continuous spacetime curve.
The positive t_min and PF-ODE endpoint encoding preserve the intended ordering of clean-data edit costs.
StabilityVAE distortion does not dominate geometry measured in EDM2 latent coordinates.
A sequence of local Langevin equilibrations along posterior distributions yields useful transition paths for the target physical system.
Maximum potential energy is an adequate proxy for transition-path quality in the alanine benchmark.
The learned two-dimensional energy surrogate and small diffusion model faithfully preserve the relevant molecular landscape.
The compared energy-evaluation counts are commensurate despite different training, optimization, and neural-model costs.

techniques.role: Shows that a same-dimensional bijective decoder with an ambient Euclidean pullback cannot create geometry beyond a coordinate change.
Measures local change in the full reverse-SDE denoising distribution rather than change in one deterministic decoded point.
Augments noisy state with diffusion time so that terminal-memorylessness collapse is avoided and curves may trade information loss against restoration.
Expresses Gaussian-corruption posteriors using explicit natural and sufficient-statistic coordinates.
Approximates continuous Fisher energy and length using adjacent natural- and expectation-coordinate differences.
Recovers posterior mean and second moment from the denoiser and its divergence.
Estimates the denoiser divergence with one Rademacher Jacobian-vector product at each curve point.
Parameterizes candidate paths with fixed-endpoint splines and minimizes discretized information energy by Adam or AdamW.
Uses optimized spacetime length as an image-pair edit cost interpreted as forgetting source-specific and adding target-specific information.
Turns a spacetime curve into a sequence of biased energy distributions and samples a molecular path by short Langevin blocks.
Adds SNR-based variance preferences and KL-based region-avoidance constraints to the path objective.

evaluations.setting: Theoretical analysis of the deterministic PF-ODE decoder under its Euclidean pullback metric.
evaluations.metric: Decoded form, length, and energy of a globally shortest latent curve.
evaluations.result: The unique decoded minimizer is the constant-speed straight segment and the minimum energy is one half the squared Euclidean endpoint distance.
evaluations.baseline: The expectation that a same-dimensional decoder pullback reveals non-Euclidean intrinsic data-manifold geometry.

evaluations.setting: Analytic one-dimensional three-component Gaussian mixture under a variance-preserving schedule.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative PF-ODE versus optimized spacetime path shape and computation time.
evaluations.result: Optimized curves are straighter at high noise and converge visually toward PF-ODE behavior near the clean endpoint; a 512-point, 2,000-step optimization takes about ten seconds on an M1 CPU.
evaluations.baseline: Three PF-ODE trajectories solved with 512 Euler steps.

evaluations.setting: EDM2 ImageNet-512 XXL latent-diffusion sampling trajectories with StabilityVAE.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative change after minimizing spacetime energy and optimization runtime.
evaluations.result: The geodesic is almost visually indistinguishable from PF-ODE, with only slightly earlier information generation; optimization takes about two A100 hours per trajectory and is not a sampler because the final endpoint is required.

evaluations.setting: Image interpolation between StabilityVAE-encoded ImageNet samples using eight-node splines, 16 evaluation points, and 200 AdamW steps.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative noise-then-denoise edit sequence and per-pair runtime.
evaluations.result: Figures show plausible transitions whose intermediate noise grows with endpoint dissimilarity; runtime is about six minutes per pair on an A100 with EDM2-XXL or about one minute with the XS model.
evaluations.baseline: No quantitative interpolation baseline, user study, or semantic-consistency metric is reported.

evaluations.setting: Two hundred random within-class ImageNet pairs drawn as 20 pairs from each of ten randomly selected classes.
evaluations.metric: Correlation of DiffED with LPIPS and SSIM.
evaluations.result: Correlation is approximately -7% with LPIPS and 53% with SSIM, without uncertainty, human ground truth, or a stated correlation statistic.
evaluations.baseline: LPIPS and SSIM as proxies for perceptual and structural similarity.

evaluations.setting: Twenty random image pairs from the ImageNet class 'Space bar.'
evaluations.metric: Qualitative pair ranking from most similar to least similar.
evaluations.result: DiffED, LPIPS, SSIM, and Euclidean distance produce visibly different rankings; no correctness criterion or observer preference is measured.
evaluations.baseline: LPIPS, SSIM, and Euclidean pixel/latent distance.

evaluations.setting: One thousand alanine-dipeptide paths in a two-dihedral-angle surrogate energy landscape.
evaluations.metric: Mean maximum surrogate energy along each path and energy-evaluation count.
evaluations.result: Spacetime geodesic reports 37.36±0.60, close to the numerical lower bound 36.42, with 16M path-generation evaluations plus 16M one-time diffusion-data evaluations; fixed-length MCMC reports 42.54±7.42/1.29B, variable-length MCMC 58.11±18.51/21.02M, and the reproduced Doob method 66.24±1.01/38.4M.
evaluations.baseline: Two MCMC shooting variants and the authors' best configuration of official Doob's Lagrangian code.

evaluations.metric: Ability to execute released alanine implementations and recover reported behavior.
evaluations.result: Holdijk is excluded due unresolved repository failures, Raja because alanine code is absent, and Doob because official code gave much worse results or NaN/straight-line collapse despite extensive tuning.
evaluations.baseline: Published Holdijk, Doob, and Raja transition-path results rather than the paper's failed or unavailable reproductions.

evaluations.setting: Low-variance and region-avoiding alanine paths with hand-tuned penalties.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative trajectory concentration and visual avoidance of a designated region.
evaluations.result: Figures show narrower paths and avoidance behavior, but no quantitative constraint satisfaction, diversity, physical validity, or objective trade-off is reported.

limitations: [Author-stated, p. 9] Nearly clean denoising distributions approach Dirac measures, making local-KL/Fisher distances effectively infinite and optimization numerically unstable; all practical endpoints therefore use non-negligible noise.
[Author-stated, p. 9] DiffED is considerably slower than established image metrics such as LPIPS and SSIM.
[Author-stated, p. 5] Endpoint-conditioned spacetime geodesics are not an alternative sampling method because the endpoint must be known in advance.

[Reviewer-identified] The pullback-collapse theorem applies specifically to a bijective same-dimensional decoder and ambient Euclidean output metric; the paper's broad 'standard pullback' rhetoric overstates its reach.
[Reviewer-identified] Approximate denoisers and stochastic divergence estimates can break the exact exponential-family dual consistency on which nonnegative pair lengths rely.
[Reviewer-identified] No estimator bias, variance, probe-count, seed, or nonnegativity study validates the single-Hutchinson-JVP approximation.
[Reviewer-identified] One locally optimized, discretized spline is not a certified global geodesic; multiple starts, convergence curves, grid refinement, and optimality bounds are absent.
[Reviewer-identified] Metric axioms are proven only for ideal globally minimized exact Fisher length, not tested for the operational approximate DiffED.
[Reviewer-identified] Practical DiffED depends on t_min, schedule, PF-ODE encoding, StabilityVAE distortion, denoiser scale, optimizer, and discretization, with no sensitivity analysis.
[Reviewer-identified] The image study contains no human perceptual judgments and DiffED has almost no agreement with LPIPS on its only quantitative sample.
[Reviewer-identified] Image correlations are point estimates over 200 within-class pairs without confidence intervals, seed disclosure, statistic definition, cross-class tests, or downstream utility.
[Reviewer-identified] The molecular study operates only on two dihedral coordinates of alanine, not full atomic dynamics or a diverse suite of molecules.

[Reviewer-identified] The original energy is replaced by a neural surrogate with reported MSE about 1.5, but path quality is evaluated on that same surrogate and error near barriers is not characterized.
[Reviewer-identified] Maximum energy alone does not establish a correct transition-path distribution, kinetics, rates, committor behavior, action, or physical diversity.
[Reviewer-identified] The strongest molecular baselines were unavailable or not reproduced, so Table 1 cannot substantiate a general state-of-the-art comparison.
[Reviewer-identified] Evaluation-count accounting excludes neural training and JVP/geodesic optimization costs and is not aligned across methods.
[Reviewer-identified] Constrained-path evidence is qualitative and depends on hand-tuned thresholds and schedules, including an extra term needed to block a trivial entropy-inflation solution.
[Reviewer-identified] The paper does not audit the linked code against the printed pseudocode typo or provide end-to-end stochastic reproducibility statistics.
failure_modes: A denoiser that is inaccurate off the training manifold can produce misleading mu values precisely where an optimizer explores for a shortcut.
Single-probe Hutchinson noise can make adjacent dual-coordinate products negative, yielding undefined square roots, noisy gradients, or optimizer-selected estimator artifacts.
Approaching t=0 drives energy large; choosing a safer t_min can change pair ordering and can make the claimed clean-data distance mostly an encoded noisy-state distance.
Cubic-spline optimization can converge to different local minima under initialization, node count, learning rate, endpoint encoding, or stochastic probe seed.
A coarse curve grid can cut across a high-cost region between evaluated nodes and underestimate length or maximum edit cost.
The VAE may identify perceptually distinct images or distort small structures, so geometry in EDM2 latent coordinates need not transfer to pixel- or human-space similarity.
Optimizing a trajectory with known endpoints cannot accelerate unconditional generation and may be more expensive than simply generating or interpolating with existing methods.
A path with low maximum surrogate energy can have incorrect kinetics, implausible time parameterization, low equilibrium probability, or insufficient ensemble diversity.
A learned energy surrogate can smooth away narrow barriers, creating artificially easy paths and invalidating both the lower bound and MaxEnergy comparison.
Annealed Langevin blocks may not mix within 128 steps; successive states can then reflect initialization lag rather than samples from the intended conditional distribution.
KL-based region avoidance can evade the penalty by increasing posterior entropy, requiring auxiliary constraints whose interaction can introduce new failure modes.
Comparing a successfully tuned new method against failed reproductions can invert method rankings without revealing which scientific assumption actually matters.
reusable_insights: Before assigning geometric meaning to a pullback, check whether the decoder is merely a bijective coordinate transformation and state exactly which output metric supplies the geometry.
Indexing conditional denoising distributions jointly by state and noise level is a reusable way to study information gained and lost across a diffusion process.
Gaussian corruption gives an unusually compact exponential-family posterior with sufficient statistic (x,||x||^2); this can remove log-partition functions from local geometry calculations.
Dual-coordinate differences turn exact exponential-family symmetrized KL into a computable curve objective and may transfer to other conditional exponential families.
Separate mathematical exactness, estimator approximation, optimization approximation, and application validation; each layer needs its own error and stability audit.
A distance implemented through optimization should ship with multiple starts, grid refinement, symmetry and triangle tests, and an uncertainty interval over estimator/optimizer randomness.
Treat t_min and representation choice as explicit hyperparameters of the operational metric and report whether rankings are stable across both.
For molecular paths, pair barrier metrics with path likelihood/action, committor or rate tests, full-coordinate physical checks, and ensemble diversity.
Baseline reproduction failures should be reported, but failed reproductions should be labeled separately from published baselines and not used alone to claim superiority.
Compute comparisons should include amortized and per-query denoiser, training, optimization, simulation, and energy-evaluation costs in a common unit.
open_questions: Can a denoiser-based projection enforce exact dual consistency or positive-semidefinite Fisher estimates when mu is approximate?
How many Hutchinson probes are needed for stable path rankings in modern latent-image dimensions, and can probes be shared or variance-reduced along a curve?
Do DiffED values converge under simultaneous refinement of t_min, curve discretization, spline complexity, optimizer restarts, and denoiser scale?
Does the operational DiffED satisfy approximate symmetry, identity, and triangle inequality, and how often do local minima violate them?
What aspects of image similarity does DiffED predict if not LPIPS or human perceptual closeness: editability, semantic change, compression rate, or diffusion transition difficulty?
Can DiffED be validated against actual human edit sequences or intervention cost rather than repurposed similarity proxies?
How does StabilityVAE distortion alter Fisher spacetime, and would pixel-space or higher-quality autoencoders change the reported rankings?
Can the geometry guide an unconditional sampler without pre-specifying the terminal data endpoint, perhaps through local direction fields or learned geodesic shooting?
Do spacetime-guided paths reproduce committors, reactive fluxes, transition rates, and path ensembles in full-atom alanine and larger proteins?
How does annealed Langevin mixing error accumulate along the curve, and can a bound connect conditional-distribution overlap to the required steps per point?
Would minimizing Onsager-Machlup action, Schrödinger-bridge cost, or path-space KL yield physically stronger paths than minimum denoising-posterior Fisher length?
Can constraint penalties be calibrated from target satisfaction probabilities instead of manually chosen rho and lambda schedules?
How do probability-density, feature-pullback, posterior-Fisher, Wasserstein, and likely-geometry paths compare under one shared interpolation and path-sampling benchmark?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding the Latent Space of Diffusion Models through the Lens of Riemannian Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. pull back a metric through U-Net encoding feature maps to obtain local latent bases and one-step image edits. Those maps and their task are not the bijective PF-ODE data decoder analyzed by the collapse theorem, so this prior is an important scope counterexample rather than a method invalidated by the paper. Spacetime instead compares full denoising posteriors across state and time.

competitive_landscape.title: Probability Density Geodesics in Image Diffusion Latent Space
competitive_landscape.difference: Yu et al. define an inverse-density inner product, solve boundary and initial value problems, analyze videos, and demonstrate training-free interpolation and extrapolation. It supplies a direct alternative notion of plausible path geometry based on density rather than denoising-posterior Fisher change and does not add a time coordinate; it should be compared quantitatively on path likelihood, interpolation, speed, and metric stability.

competitive_landscape.title: Hessian Geometry of Latent Space in Generative Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Lobashev et al. reconstruct the log-partition Hessian/Fisher metric from posterior samples, provide convergence results, and study phase transitions in statistical-physics and diffusion models. Spacetime exploits Gaussian corruption for explicit posterior coordinates and optimized paths, while Hessian Geometry focuses on learned latent families, phase boundaries, and metric reconstruction.

competitive_landscape.title: A Likely Geometry of Generative Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Rygaard et al. construct a general probability-compatible pseudo-metric, derive a Newtonian/Riemannian correspondence, and compute density-seeking shortest paths and generalized Fréchet means across model families without retraining. It is broader and avoids reverse-SDE posterior geometry; Spacetime supplies a diffusion-specific information interpretation and transition-path construction.

competitive_landscape.title: Geometry of Score Based Generative Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Ghimire et al. characterize forward and backward score-based processes as Wasserstein gradient flows and add projection for faster sampling. That is optimal-transport geometry over distributions and targets sampler efficiency, whereas Spacetime uses Fisher geometry of endpoint-conditioned denoising distributions and cannot sample without a known endpoint.

competitive_landscape.title: Image generation with shortest path diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Das et al. optimize the forward corruption process using Fisher path length and report improved generation from the resulting sharpening/noise-deblurring schedule. It directly modifies an operational sampler, unlike endpoint-conditioned reverse spacetime; its distribution-level assumptions and forward-process objective differ from the posterior-family metric here.

competitive_landscape.title: Doob's Lagrangian: A Sample-Efficient Variational Approach to Transition Path Sampling
competitive_landscape.difference: Du et al. optimize a simulation-free variational Doob h-transform with endpoint conditions and validate on molecular and protein-folding tasks; v4 explicitly updates alanine results after fixing unphysical parameterization and energy computation. Spacetime reports much worse performance from official code and compares to that failed reproduction, but only tests a two-angle surrogate alanine system and a maximum-energy metric.

competitive_landscape.title: Transition Path Sampling with Improved Off-Policy Training of Diffusion Path Samplers
competitive_landscape.difference: TPS-DPS trains an amortized path sampler by log-variance divergence with control variates, replay buffers, off-policy learning, and equivariant bias forces, then evaluates synthetic systems, a small peptide, and fast-folding proteins for realism and diversity. It is training-heavy but offers substantially broader physical validation than the one-system, one-metric Spacetime experiment.

competitive_landscape.title: Action-Minimization Meets Generative Modeling: Efficient Transition Path Sampling with the Onsager-Machlup Functional
competitive_landscape.difference: Raja et al. minimize Onsager-Machlup action under pretrained diffusion or flow dynamics and report diverse, physically realistic paths across varied molecules, including generalization beyond training data. Spacetime excludes it from alanine comparison because released code lacked that experiment, but the current paper is a direct, broader competitor whose action-based physical objective should be compared against Fisher-length guidance.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Latent Diffusability via Fisher Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: Gu et al. decompose MMSE rate into Fisher-information and Fisher-information-rate terms and identify compression, tangential distortion, encoder curvature, and intrinsic-data-curvature penalties across autoencoders. This is especially relevant because Spacetime relies on StabilityVAE coordinates without analyzing representation distortion; it studies when latent diffusion geometry is preserved rather than constructing endpoint geodesics.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first unified Fisher-Rao geometry on diffusion spacetime, an exponential-family simulation-free curve estimator, a principled Diffusion Edit Distance, and competitive constrained transition-path sampling.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact exponential-family coordinates for p(x0|xt), their use across the augmented state-time domain, and the dual-coordinate curve objective form a distinctive technical package. The applications include an operational image distance and conditional-Boltzmann annealing along optimized curves.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The spacetime posterior-family formulation and tractable dual-coordinate derivation are genuinely novel and technically valuable. The broad dismissal of pullback geometry is over-scoped, operational DiffED is not yet validated as a metric or useful image distance, and transition-path superiority is not established beyond one reduced surrogate benchmark with failed baseline reproductions. The strongest research opportunity is to preserve the formal construction while adding estimator-consistency guarantees, certified or uncertainty-aware path optimization, and physically meaningful multi-system validation against density, action, Doob, and path-space methods.

reviewer_notes: Read all 25 pages of the current arXiv v4 / ICLR 2026 Oral paper, including proofs, algorithms, experimental appendices, baseline-reproducibility note, and printed JAX listing. Numerical values were checked against the extracted full text. Competitive review was refreshed on 2026-08-23 against current primary arXiv records for diffusion pullback/density/Fisher/Wasserstein geometries and modern Doob, diffusion-path, and Onsager-Machlup transition samplers. Reviewer inferences explicitly distinguish exact results from estimator, optimizer, and application evidence.
